REQ-1.description: Orchestration Protocol v1 is a versioned public contract, separate from the Workflow release and the governing version: one CLI, one JSON response envelope, a protocol version whose unknown major fails closed, broad stable error codes alongside the precise Workflow-native exception, and a describe operation reporting release, protocol version, supported governing versions and capabilities.

REQ-2.description: verify reports repository, state and protocol health without writing: state and config readable and valid (validate_state's first production caller), registry and mirror consistent, checkpoint completions provable, and the installed release record agreeing with the script's own release.

REQ-3.description: next-action returns, for every persisted phase and governing version, a normalized snapshot, a semantic action id with arguments and a rendered invocation, one disposition (automatic, validation, human_gate, external_gate, blocked, complete), generic worker requirements, allowed result classes, and the decision basis (state revision and state identity); a decision taken on a basis that no longer matches the state is refused as stale.

REQ-4.description: reconcile classifies the durable result of an executed automatic action against its decision as progress, no_progress, gate_reached or invalid, recognizing same-phase progress such as a checkpoint completing while the phase stays IMPLEMENTING, and returns the new decision basis; a gate decision is refused, and completion is reported by next-action's complete disposition.

REQ-5.description: record-external-result ingests a manual external plan or implementation review verdict: the Workflow parses the verdict header, checks its binding to the current bundle and review_content_id, stores it at the Workflow-resolved feedback path and records the stage, through the same single function the record-manual commands call; unsupported result kinds are refused.

REQ-6.description: resolve-artifact returns the Workflow-resolved path of a named semantic artifact kind for a work item, so no consumer copies feedback, bundle or plan-input path rules.

REQ-7.description: One review_content_id label is pinned in REVIEW_PROTOCOL.md's required feedback structure and written by both review commands; the parser accepts the other historical label as a legacy alias and still refuses two distinct values.

REQ-8.description: Plan-stage content once taken out of review (withdrawn, or consumed by a REVISE or a plan amendment) is recorded durably and can never be published or bound again; 2.6.0 single-slot records migrate without loss of their slot, and the withdraw, detour, restore sequence is refused.

REQ-9.description: Workflow 2.7.0 is releasable: the manifest lists every new and changed file with its digest at version 2.7.0, the release-source conformance CI and the shipped conformance template run the new suite, and the protocol's release constant must equal the manifest version for a build to succeed.

REQ-10.description: The protocol is specified in a shipped normative document with every operation's request and response shape, and the command and operator documents agree with the new behaviour; an end-to-end test drives a disposable repository through the lifecycle using only protocol responses.

REQ-11.description: A two-stage REVISE is applied by content: apply-plan-review and apply-implementation-review accept a REVISE that states the reviewed review_content_id whatever its advisory bundle fields say, refuse one that states other content even when its bundle fields name the current bundle, and check the on-disk bundle against its own manifest, including that the manifest names this work item and stage, which takes the place of a Work item field the verdict may omit (a manifest that names no work item keeps the bundle binding); no catalogue remedy rewrites a reviewer's binding fields.
